First public release of dpi-for-everyone: get past SNI-based DPI
filtering without a VPN, a remote server or any per-application
configuration.

## Linux — automatic transparent mode

```sh
git clone https://github.com/kadireren7/dpi-for-everyone.git
cd dpi-for-everyone
sudo ./scripts/install.sh
```

One command, then blocked HTTPS sites and apps just work — in every
browser and application, with no proxy settings and no DNS changes.

- **System-wide HTTPS interception** via nftables and a local
  transparent proxy.
- **DNS-over-HTTPS protection:** every DNS query, including queries to
  the router, is answered through an internal DoH forwarder, so blocked
  names resolve to real addresses instead of block pages.
- **TLS record fragmentation:** the TLS ClientHello is re-framed into
  two records split inside the server name (with an optional TCP
  split), found automatically per network.
- **Automatic decisions:** known-blocked services (Discord and others)
  are bypassed from the first connection; other sites are tried
  normally and a bypass is learned only when needed, per site and per
  network, after certificate verification.
- **QUIC fallback:** QUIC to bypassed destinations is rejected so
  applications fall back to TCP.
- **systemd integration and automatic startup** at boot.
- **Fail-open:** if the service stops or fails, interception ends by
  itself and the connection keeps working unbypassed.
- **Lightweight CLI:** `dpi-proxy-ctl status | logs | strategy | restart
  | stop`. A few MB of memory, a handful of threads.

Tested on real residential networks where Discord and other HTTPS
services are DPI-blocked: they load with no proxy or DNS
configuration.

## Windows and macOS

The binaries below are a local SOCKS5 proxy (`127.0.0.1:1080`); set
`DPI_PROXY_SPLIT_TLS=record` to enable TLS record fragmentation. No
system-wide interception and no DNS protection on these platforms.

## Known limitations

- Not a VPN: IP-address blocks and region blocks are not bypassed.
- HTTPS (TCP/443) and DNS only; voice/video/game UDP traffic is not
  handled.
- Effectiveness depends on the network's DPI; not guaranteed against
  every censorship system.
- Never decrypts TLS; do not run it alongside another transparent DPI
  tool.

## Assets

- `dpi-proxy-linux-x86_64` — Linux binary (the installer builds from
  source; this is for SOCKS5 use or inspection)
- `dpi-proxy-macos-arm64`, `dpi-proxy-windows-x86_64.exe` — SOCKS5 proxy
- `SHA256SUMS`
